pr_title: Check Annotations map against nil for ConfigMapLock#Update()
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
As #87800 reported, in some scenario when ConfigMapLock#Update() is called, the Annotations map is not allocated, leading to panic.

This PR allocates the map if needed.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #87800

**Special notes for your reviewer**:


```release-note
NONE
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

```docs

```
pr_comments: /test pull-kubernetes-integration
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce-device-plugin-gpu

Can we add at least a trivial test that would have broken without this change? Seems like it should be easy to trigger the bad path.

/assign @caesarxuchao
I'm curious how #87800 was triggered.

At a glance it seems highly likely that the right solution is that all of these methods need to be protected by a sync.Mutex, or the documentation should note that it is not valid to access a ConfigMapLock from multiple goroutines.
It seems if we check cml.cm.Annotations before accessing its entries, the race condition should be taken care of - hence, Mutex may not be needed.

@tedyu can you check what's the use case that leads to the race? I think the resourceLock is not designed to be thread-safe in the first place.

Also, no matter what we decide as the proper fix, we need to apply it to the other resource lock implementations as well.

> It seems if we check cml.cm.Annotations before accessing its entries, the race condition should be taken care of - hence, Mutex may not be needed.

This is definitely not true: nothing stops someone from calling Get() twice on a single ConfigMapLock, and if Get() and Update() can be concurrent, then between Update checking for nil and dereferencing the Annotations, they could become nil again. (Likewise, if Update and Get are concurrent, the Update might not be updating the annotations on the ConfigMap the caller thought it was!)

Probably @caesarxuchao is right and this object is not useful for concurrent access anyway, in which case a comment to that effect is more useful than a lock.

> I'm curious how #87800 was triggered.

I just deleted my controllers RBAC permission to update configmaps (it still had `get` permisson, if it matters) and then waiting for it to lose the lock and it crashes.

@jktomer 
From ConfigMapLock#Get
```
	cml.cm, err = cml.Client.ConfigMaps(cml.ConfigMapMeta.Namespace).Get(cml.ConfigMapMeta.Name, metav1.GetOptions{})
```
Instead of assigning to cml.cm directly, we can store the ConfigMap pointer in a variable. After filling in cm.Annotations, we assign the cm to cml.cm

But I agree ConfigMapLock is not thread safe.
I have a reproduction in a unit test. You can check it out at https://github.com/istio/istio/blob/df198c22bb8536a4ed09ac7f32caaaafb45ef961/pilot/pkg/leaderelection/leaderelection_test.go#L95.
Also will this be backported to 1.17? Just want to know if we should wait for a fix or look into an alternative for the short term

@jktomer @caesarxuchao 
I want to get your opinion on which approach you favor:
1. what this PR currently presents
2. make the assignment to cml.cm more robust, as described in:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/87821#issuecomment-582171124

thanks

The panic I see when running @howardjohn's test is not in ConfigMapLock.Update() but in ConfigMapLock.RecordEvent(), which incorrectly assumes that cml.cm is non-nil; that's a separate bug.

The panic in #87800 does look like a concurrency problem:

1. LeaderElector.renew() spawns a goroutine that calls LeaderElector.tryAcquireOrRenew()
1. It then selects on tryAcquireOrRenew() finishing or a timeout
1. tryAcquireOrRenew() calls ConfigMapLock.Get()
1. If the timeout fires, renew() will call LeaderElection.release() if ReleaseOnCancel is true
1. LeaderElection.release() calls ConfigMapLock.Update()

Since ConfigMapLock.Get() involves an actual HTTP request exactly one line before allocating Annotations, this is a very plausible-looking data race.

Adding a lock around all ConfigMapLock's mutating methods will prevent this panic and any number of other data-race bugs that are surely present, but will have the effect of making LeaderElector.Run() possibly block for a long time after its context is cancelled; making Update() nonblocking (having it return an error if it can't acquire the lock) seems worse, though.

@jktomer 
The sequence you described above was plausible.
I hinted at this scenario in:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/87821#discussion_r374932060

Adding lock around related methods seems like a proper fix.

@caesarxuchao 
What do you think ?
w.r.t. ConfigMapLock#RecordEvent accessing cml.cm unconditionally, I can fix it in this PR as well.
Ah yeah, just realized that was a different issue. I'll see if I can get a unit test for the original issue as well

I tested this in a live deployment and its fixed with this change. I couldn't reproduce the race in the unit test though, not sure why its different there when I can hit it 100% of the time in cluster

I was waiting for @jktomer to confirm the locking approach.

So @tedyu's original fix actually happened to be right. @tedyu can you copy what https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84801/files#diff-aec6f9eb96effc3f6d7825d38f4a7ffd to configmap lock. It looks like the leaselock.go doesn't have this issue, but please double check. Thanks!

review_comments:
Based on the comment on line 80, the method should return an error if annotation doesn't exist.

OTOH, this won't happen because cml.cm is initialized at line 68, which populate the annotations.
In Update, it seems we can error out if cml.cm.Annotations == nil.

Per my comment in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84801#issuecomment-601905313, when `Update` fails, we store an empty `*v1.ConfigMap` in the "cm" field. It doesn't require a race or any concurrency. It's due to the mistaken assumption that `Update` would have returned a more complete struct value.
